statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail holds at 20% at the bottom of the watch band as NQ stabilises around 30,878 without reclaiming the 31,094.75 pivot, while a fourth consecutive rise in the 10-year yield to 5.32% and Brent above 100 dollars keep Stress at 75%.
recommendation: Tail is unchanged at 20% and remains five points below the 25% block threshold. The preceding assessment identified the deep retracement off 31,147.75 as the reason Tail stepped back into the lower watch band; that read is confirmed rather than reversed this hour. NQ has recovered roughly 49 points from the 30,829 print of the previous assessment to 30,878.25, which is a partial bounce inside the fade rather than a resumption: price remains about 270 points below the overnight high and about 216 points below the 31,094.75 pivot. No Tail amplifier is observed. There is no session-extreme holding, no shallow-pullback sequence and no repeated extension after a failed retracement. Mapped policy state is WATCH. The 12:00-15:00Z danger window covering jobless claims, Fed's Barkin, the cash open, the final manufacturing PMI and ISM manufacturing is unchanged and remains the hour range where observed post-release continuation would justify escalation.
headline: NQ steadies near 30,878 inside the overnight fade, holding Tail at 20% while Brent clears 100 dollars and the 10-year yield rises a fourth session to 5.32%
body: December E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures trade 30,878.25, up 179.50 points or 0.58% from the 30,698.75 settle, with a session range of 30,684.50 to 31,147.75 on about 125.04k contracts. A second independent source corroborates at 30,876.00, up 177.25 points or 0.58%, on 125,053 contracts, so the level is well established across venues. The development of this hour is consolidation rather than direction. The previous assessment recorded 30,829.00 after roughly 319 points of the 449-point overnight advance had been retraced; price has since recovered about 49 points, which leaves the retracement overwhelmingly intact. NQ sits roughly 270 points below the 31,147.75 overnight high and roughly 216 points below the 31,094.75 pivot that earlier assessments named as the marker of genuine uptrend resumption. A bounce of that proportion inside a fade of that depth is the ordinary two-way behaviour of a functioning book, and it is the structural opposite of the no-retracement path the Tail score is built to detect. The overnight catalyst has now been absorbed. Micron reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of 54.23 billion dollars against 51.07 billion expected and adjusted earnings of 33.42 dollars against 31.61 expected, guided first-quarter revenue to about 61.5 billion dollars, and still closed the after-hours session only 0.16% higher. An exceptional beat that produces a muted reaction is evidence that positioning was already long the theme, which argues for range behaviour rather than for a second directional leg. Cross-asset conditions are the reason Stress stays high at 75% while Tail stays low. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.32%, up about three basis points and rising for a fourth consecutive session, near its highest in roughly nineteen years; the Federal Reserve H.15 series corroborates the trend, with the 10-year moving from 5.11% on 23 September to 5.26% on 29 September. The 2-year is 4.91%, so the curve continues to bear-steepen. Brent trades 100.19 dollars, up 2.20%, and WTI 92.38 dollars, up 2.17%, firming on an unresolved US-Iran impasse with OPEC+ expected to leave November quotas unchanged. Equities rising while the long end sells off and crude pushes through 100 dollars is a cross-asset conflict, and under the operative risk definition a conflict of that kind raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. VIX at 16.68, up 2.08%, is consistent with that reading: the move is higher but the absolute level remains low and gives no support to a pathological-path score. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and was not used as material evidence. Its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly 34 hours old and well outside the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collection status is partial. Stale supporting context cannot establish current structure, so this assessment rests entirely on independent current research. The day ahead is dense. September Challenger job cuts were scheduled for 09:30Z with consensus near 78.0K against a 52.881K prior, and that outcome is not yet confirmed within this assessment. Initial and continuing jobless claims follow at 12:30Z with consensus near 195K after a 197K prior, Fed's Barkin speaks at 13:05Z, the cash open is at 13:30Z, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI prints at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus a touch above the 54.6 prior. September non-farm payrolls follow tomorrow at 12:30Z, outside this forecast window. None of these scheduled items is treated as an automatic Tail escalation. The 7 August precedent is directly on point: a large payrolls surprise did not become a lethal no-retracement path, so event importance and dispersion are scored through Stress and Confidence until observed price action says otherwise. Confidence is 88%. Current NQ levels are corroborated across two sources, yields are confirmed against both a live feed and the Federal Reserve H.15 release, oil and VIX carry current quotes, the Micron result is verified, and the seven-day calendar is checked. The only material gap is the stale shared context file, which is a small completeness deduction against an otherwise current evidence set.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 15-16% through the European and early US hours of 30 September with the mode mixed, stepped into the watch band at 20% from 12:00Z as the US data block and the long-end selloff developed, and peaked at 23% around 15:00-16:00Z. It held 20-22% through the US afternoon and the early Asian session, then firmed steadily from 20% at 00:00Z through 21%, 22% and 23% to 24% at 05:00Z and 25% at 06:00Z as NQ printed successive fresh overnight highs and accepted above the 31,094.75 pivot, with the mode turning trend-up across those two slots. The 07:00Z slot returned to 22% and the mixed mode once the first liquid two-way test produced a 188-point retracement, and 08:00Z returned to 20% as that retracement deepened to 319 points on expanding turnover. Stress rose steadily across the period from 65% to 75%, and Confidence held 85-88% throughout.
outlookSummary: The danger window is unchanged at 12:00-15:00Z, covering initial and continuing jobless claims at 12:30Z against consensus near 195K after 197K, Fed's Barkin at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open, the final S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 13:45Z and ISM manufacturing plus August construction spending at 14:00Z with ISM consensus near 54.7 against a 54.6 prior. Forecast Tail opens at 20% and holds there across the mid-European hours where the deepest pre-US book normally extends rather than truncates a retracement, firms to 21-22% into the claims hour and the cash open, and peaks at the top of the watch band at 24% across the 14:00Z ISM hour where Stress tops at 79%. It decays to 20-22% through the US afternoon, the 20:00Z cash close and the late evening, where Stress reaches its forecast-day low of 71%. It then firms through the Asian session and the European pre-open to 23-24% as positioning concentrates ahead of September non-farm payrolls at 12:30Z on 2 October, which falls outside this 24-hour window. The whole forecast path stays inside the watch band and no slot reaches the 25% block threshold, because scheduled event importance and dispersion are scored through Stress and Confidence rather than through Tail until an observed price path establishes mean-reversion failure. Confidence decays from 88% to 82% with forecast distance and recovers slightly to 84% once European cash hours restore observable structure.
